NONE: A1 used especially in questions as the subject or object of a verb, when asking which person or people, or when asking what someone's name is
› used with verbs that relate to knowing, when you want to say that something is not known
（與表示「知道」的動詞連用，表示不知道）
A2 used as the subject or object of a verb to show which person you are referring to, or to add information about a person just mentioned. It is used for people, not things
（用作動詞的主詞或受詞，表示所提及的人，或附加所提及的人的資訊）

example: Who did this?
這是誰做的？
Who's she?
她是誰？
Who are all those people?
那些人是誰？
She asked me if I knew who had got the job.
她問我是否知道誰獲得了那份工作。
Who (also formal whom) do you want to talk to?
您要找哪位？
I don't know who to ask to the party.
我不知道該邀請誰參加聚會。
"Are they going to get married?" "Who knows?" (= It is not possible to know at the moment.)
「他們是要結婚了嗎？」「誰知道呢。」
Who can tell what will happen now?
誰知道會發生甚麼呢？
I think it was your dad who phoned.
我認為打電話的人是你爸爸。
She's one of those people who love to be the centre of attention.
她是那種喜歡引人注意的人。
He called James, who was a good friend as well as the family doctor.
他打電話給詹姆斯，詹姆斯既是家庭醫生又是他的好朋友。
The other people who (also that) live in the house are really friendly.
其他住在這所房子裡的人十分友好。
This is Gabriel, who I told you about.
這是加布裡埃爾，我跟你說起過他。
"Is it possible?" "Who can say?"
「這可能嗎?」「誰知道？」

NONE: › used to mean that the thing referred to is not necessary or useful, or causes trouble

example: Men! Who needs them?
男人，誰稀罕他們？

NONE: › used when you are telling people about a bad thing that someone else has done
（說起某人做的壞事時）不便說出其名的

example: One boy, who shall remain nameless, has been late every day this week.
有一個男孩本周每天都遲到，這裡就不說他的名字了。

NONE: C2 used to say that you are very surprised something has happened

example: So, Alex is going out with Hannah. Who would have thought it?
那麼，亞曆克斯在與漢娜約會。誰會想得到呢？
She wondered who'd sent her the mysterious email.
她想知道是誰給她發的神秘電子郵件。
Well, who'd have thought Joey was going to become so successful?
誰會想到喬伊會變得如此成功？
Who'll be at the party tomorrow?
明天有誰去參加聚會？
Who's been chosen, do you know?
你知道誰被選中了嗎？
Who's that talking to Jason?
那個跟賈森談話的人是誰？

NONE: › the people who are most important in a particular group
（某組織中各人的職位和工作）每人的情況，誰是誰
› a book containing information about the world's richest or most famous people

example: The guest list reads like a Who's Who of top American businessmen.
賓客名單讀起來像是美國巨賈豪商的名人錄。
Who've you asked so far?
目前為止你都問過誰了？

NONE: › used when telling a horse to stop
› informal used when telling a person to stop what they are doing or to do it more slowly

example: "Whoa there, Poppy," he said to his pony, and stopped beside the kerb.
「咳，波皮。」他向自己的小馬喝道，扯扯韁繩停在路邊。
Yes, carrots please, - whoa! That's plenty.
是的，要些胡蘿蔔，——好了！這就足夠了。

NONE: › a story about a crime and the attempt to discover who committed it

example: It's one of those whodunnits where you don't find out who the murderer is till the very end.
這是那種直到最後才能找出殺人兇手的偵探小說。

NONE: › used in questions as a way of expressing surprise
（表示驚訝）究竟是誰，到底是誰

example: Whoever uprooted that tree ought to be ashamed of themselves.
把樹連根拔起的那個人應當感到羞恥。
Could I speak to whoever is in charge of International Sales, please?
能找負責國際銷售的人接電話嗎？
Can whoever leaves last please lock the door?
最後走的人請鎖門好嗎？
He says he bought the car from Frank, whoever Frank is. (= I do not know who Frank is.)
他說自己是從弗蘭克那裡買的車，不知道這個弗蘭克是誰。
Whoever told you that?
到底是誰告訴你的？
Whoever could that be phoning at this time?
這個時候打電話來到底是誰呢？

NONE: C2 as a single object and not in pieces

example: I spent the whole day cleaning.
我花了一整天打掃衛生。
There's still a whole month till my birthday.
離我的生日還有整整一個月時間。
After my exercise class, my whole body ached.
體育課之後，我渾身都痛。
The whole town was destroyed by the earthquake.
地震摧毀了整個城鎮。
This whole thing (= situation) is ridiculous.
這一切太荒謬了。
Bill does nothing but complain the whole time (= all the time).
比爾什麼都沒做，一直在抱怨。
You have to stand up in court and promise to tell "the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth".
你必須站在法庭上宣誓：「事實，全部事實，只有事實。」
Her dance compositions added a whole (= completely) new dimension to the contemporary dance repertoire.
她的舞蹈作品為現代舞劇目增添了全新的內容。
I have a whole pile of work to do this afternoon.
我今天下午有一大堆工作要做。
The new computers are a whole lot (= much) faster.
新電腦的速度要快得多了。
The seeds can be eaten whole or ground in a coffee grinder.
這些豆子可以整個吃，也可以用咖啡機磨成粉。
Now he's arrived, it's a whole different situation.
現在他來了，情況就完全不同了。
Two halves make a whole.
兩個一半構成一個整體。
You should consider each problem as an aspect of the whole.
你必須把每個問題作為整體的一個方面來考慮。
I'll be on holiday the whole of next week.
下週一整週我都要休假。
The whole of his finger was bruised.
他整根手指都腫了。
The whole of the school (= everyone in the school) had come to the fair.
全校的人都來參加展覽會了。

NONE: › food that has not had any of its natural features taken away or any artificial substances added
（不含人工添加劑的）全天然食品，全營養食品

example: a wholefood shop
全營養食品商店

NONE: › a musical note with a time value equal to two minims or four crotchets
› a number, such as 1, 3, or 17, that has no fractions and no digits after the decimal point
› the largest difference in pitch between two notes that are next to each other in the western musical scale

example: The interval from G to A is a whole step.
從 G 到 A 的音程是一個全音。
Compare
half step

NONE: › (of particular types of food) containing whole seeds

example: The minister has pledged his wholehearted support for the plans.
部長表示將全心全意支持這個計劃。

NONE: › (of flour or food made from flour) containing all the natural features of the grain, with nothing taken away
› of or for the selling of goods in large amounts at low prices to shops and businesses, rather than the selling of goods in shops to customers
› often disapproving (especially of something bad or too extreme) complete or affecting a lot of things, people, places, etc.
（尤指壞事或過於極端的事）完全的（地），大規模的（地）
› the price at which goods are sold to shops by the people who produce them, rather than the price which the customer usually pays in the shop

example: a wholesale supplier/business
批發供應商／業務
We only sell wholesale, not to the public.
我們只批發，不零售。
Compare
retail noun
I bought my coat direct from the factory at wholesale.
我的大衣是按批發價直接從廠家購買的。

NONE: › someone who buys and sells goods in large amounts to shops and businesses

example: a furniture wholesaler
傢俱批發商

NONE: › good for you, and likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally

example: good, wholesome family entertainment
優質有益的家庭娛樂
He looks like a nice, wholesome young man.
他看起來是個善良而又健康向上的年輕人。

NONE: › (of flour or food made from flour) containing all the natural features of the grain, with nothing taken away

example: I wasn't wholly convinced by her explanation.
她的解釋未能令我完全信服。
That's a wholly different issue.
那完全是另一回事。
a machine that is wholly British-made
完全由英國製造的一臺機器

NONE: › relating to a company that is completely owned by another company or organization
（公司）完全被另一公司擁有的
B2 used instead of "who" as the object of a verb or preposition

example: I met a man with whom I used to work.
我碰見了個過去曾一起工作的人。
He took out a photo of his son, whom he adores.
他拿出了一張愛子的照片。
There were 500 passengers, of whom 121 drowned.
500名乘客中共有121名溺水生亡。
To whom do you wish to speak?
你想找誰接電話？

NONE: whoever (PERSON) when used as the object
› to give a loud, excited shout, especially to show your enjoyment of or agreement with something
（尤指為表示高興或贊同而）吶喊，大叫
› a loud, excited shout, especially showing your enjoyment of or agreement with something
（尤指表示高興或贊同的）吶喊，大叫

example: The audience was whooping and clapping.
觀眾們在歡呼鼓掌。
See also
whooping cough
When the whoops and cheers had finally died down he started to speak.
當歡呼聲平息下來的時候，他開始講話。

NONE: › to enjoy yourself in a noisy and excited way
› said when you do not think what someone has said or done is important or special
哈哈（對某人說的話或做的事表示輕蔑）

example: Well, whoop-de-doo, they're offering us a 0.5 percent pay raise!
噢，哈哈，他們給我們漲了0.5%的工資！

NONE: › a loud, excited shout of happiness

example: Whoopee, it's the holidays!
哈哈，假期來了！

NONE: › a disease, common especially in children, that causes severe coughing
› an expression of surprise or feeling sorry about a mistake or slight accident
哎喲（表示驚訝或後悔的感嘆聲）

example: Whoops! That's the second time I've spilled coffee today!
哎呀！這都是我今天第二次把咖啡弄灑了！

C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] a soft sound made by something moving fast through the air or like that made when air is pushed out of something
S: › [ S ] a sudden fast movement of a liquid or air
短時間內感受（或收到的）大量某物

NONE: › to move along quickly, making a soft sound like the wind
嗖嗖（呼呼）地飛快移動；發出嗖嗖（呼呼）聲
› used to describe something that happens very fast, with no pauses or delay
（表示突然猛衝或飛速行進發出的聲音）嗖，呼

example: The train sped through the station with a whoosh.
火車呼嘯著飛速駛過車站。
I felt a great whoosh of adrenalin.
我突然感到一陣興奮。
A fast motorboat whooshed by.
一艘快艇嗖地一聲飛馳而過。
No sooner had she arrived than, whoosh, she was off again.
她沒到一會兒，嗖地一下，又離開了。
She whopped him with her handbag.
她用手袋打他。

NONE: › humorous informal something that is surprising because it is so much bigger than the usual size

example: My nose is pretty big, but my Dad's got a whopper.
我的鼻子已經很大了，而我爸爸的鼻子更大。
Amanda's told some whoppers in her time.
阿曼達曾撒過一些大謊。
She had a whopping great bruise on her arm.
她胳膊上有一大片瘀傷。
a whopping 35 percent pay rise
35%的巨大工資漲幅
a whopping lie
彌天大謊

NONE: › offensive a woman whose behaviour in her sexual relationships is considered immoral

example: The film begins with a young couple who're just about to get married.
電影一開始講的是一對即將結婚的青年男女。

NONE: › a circular pattern of lines, with the smallest circle in the middle, surrounded by other circles, each one wider and larger than the previous one
B1 used especially in questions when asking about which person owns or is responsible for something
B1 used for adding information about a person or thing just mentioned
（用於附加所提及的人或物的資訊）

example: Whose is this bag?
這是誰的袋子？
Whose bag is this?
這個袋子是誰的？
There was a picture in the paper of a man whose leg had been blown off.
報紙上有一張照片，照片中那個男人的腿被炸掉了。
They meet in an old house, whose basement has been converted into a chapel.
他們在一所舊房子裡見面，那所房子的地下室已經被改建成一個小禮拜堂。
Fraud detectives are investigating the company, three of whose senior executives have already been arrested.
反詐騙偵探正在調查那家公司，該公司的三名高級管理人員已被拘捕。

NONE: › an enthusiastic fan of the BBC television programme "Dr. Who"
（BBC電視節目）《超時空奇俠》的劇迷

example: An avid Whovian, the actor was thrilled to be offered a part in the show.
這名演員，同時也是《超時空奇俠》的劇迷，得到了出演劇中角色的機會，欣喜若狂。
